_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from Element Web's documentation; no upstream egg.
name: Element Web
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Element Web is the Matrix chat client in the browser. The egg serves it with Caddy and points it at your homeserver, with no integration manager or bug reports sent anywhere else.
startup: if [ -n "{{HOMESERVER_URL}}" ]; then n="{{HOMESERVER_NAME}}"; [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "{{HOMESERVER_URL}}" | sed -E 's#^https?://##; s#[:/].*##'); jq --arg u "{{HOMESERVER_URL}}" --arg n "$n" '.default_server_config["m.homeserver"] = {base_url: $u, server_name: $n}' config.json > config.json.new && mv -f config.json.new config.json || { rm -f config.json.new; echo "config.json isn't valid JSON, so the homeserver wasn't set in it."; }; fi; exec ./caddy run --config Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Element Web: downloads Element from its GitHub releases and Caddy, the
# web server that serves it, from Caddy's, both checked against GitHub's
# SHA-256. config.json and the Caddyfile are never touched once there, and
# the app is only replaced once the new one is complete.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Caddy has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag element-hq/element-web "$version") || exit 1
caddy=$(gh-release tag caddyserver/caddy latest) || exit 1

if [ -x caddy ] && [ "$(cat .caddy-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$caddy" ]; then
    echo "Caddy $caddy is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Caddy $caddy"
    gh-release download caddyserver/caddy "$caddy" "caddy_${caddy#v}_linux_${arch}.tar.gz" "$work/caddy.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/caddy.tar.gz" -C "$work" caddy
    install -m 0755 "$work/caddy" caddy.new
    mv -f caddy.new caddy
    echo "$caddy" > .caddy-version
fi

if [ -f element/index.html ] && [ "$(cat .element-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Element $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Element $tag"
    gh-release download element-hq/element-web "$tag" "element-$tag.tar.gz" "$work/element.tar.gz"
    mkdir -p "$work/element"
    tar -xzf "$work/element.tar.gz" -C "$work/element" --strip-components=1
    [ -f "$work/element/index.html" ] || fail "Element's download didn't have the app in it. Reinstall to try again."
    # Element's own sample settings stay in the app's folder; yours are
    # config.json next to it.
    rm -f "$work/element/config.json"
    rm -rf element.old
    [ ! -d element ] || mv element element.old
    mv "$work/element" element
    rm -rf element.old
    echo "$tag" > .element-version
fi

if [ ! -f config.json ]; then
    # Element's settings: https://github.com/element-hq/element-web/blob/develop/docs/config.md
    # The homeserver comes from the server's settings at every start. No
    # integration manager or bug report address: nothing is sent to anyone
    # but your homeserver unless you add them.
    cat > config.json <<'JSON'
{
    "default_server_config": {
        "m.homeserver": {
            "base_url": "https://matrix.org",
            "server_name": "matrix.org"
        }
    },
    "brand": "Element",
    "disable_guests": true,
    "disable_3pid_login": false,
    "integrations_ui_url": "",
    "integrations_rest_url": "",
    "integrations_widgets_urls": [],
    "show_labs_settings": false,
    "room_directory": {
        "servers": []
    }
}
JSON
fi
if [ ! -f Caddyfile ]; then
    cat > Caddyfile <<'CADDY'
# Caddy's settings: https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile
# Serves Element from the element folder on the server's port, with your
# config.json. Restart the server after changing this file.
{
	admin off
	log {
		format console
	}
}

:{$SERVER_PORT} {
	encode
	header {
		X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN
		X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
		X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block"
		Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self'"
	}
	@fresh path / /index.html /config.json /version /i18n/* /sw.js
	header @fresh Cache-Control "no-cache"
	handle /config.json {
		root * .
		file_server
	}
	handle {
		root * element
		file_server
	}
}
CADDY
fi
echo "Installed Element $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Element Web version to install, such as 1.12.35, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Homeserver address
variables.description: The address of the Matrix homeserver Element signs in to, starting with https.

variables.name: Homeserver name
variables.description: The server name in your users' Matrix IDs, such as example.com. Empty uses the homeserver address's host.
